q: Name the Army Values.
a: Loyalty, Duty, Respect, Selfless Service, Honor, Integrity, Personal Courage. LDRSHIP.

q: What are the two basic responsibilities of an NCO?
a: Accomplishment of the mission and the welfare of Soldiers. (NCO Creed, paragraph 2)

q: What is the Warrior Ethos?
a: I will always place the mission first. I will never accept defeat. I will never quit. I will never leave a fallen comrade.

q: What publication covers Army leadership and the profession?
a: ADP 6-22, Army Leadership and the Profession.

q: Which Army Value is the hardest for you to live, and why?
a: Pick one honestly, such as selfless service when you're tired. Give an example and what you do about it.

q: What does "time honored corps" mean to you?
a: The NCO Corps dates to 1775. It's a tradition of leaders who carry out the mission and take care of Soldiers. Now you're joining it.

q: Define integrity.
a: Do what is right, legally and morally. Being honest in word and deed, even when no one is watching.

q: Define selfless service.
a: Put the welfare of the Nation, the Army and your subordinates before your own.

q: Define personal courage.
a: Face fear, danger or adversity, both physical and moral.

q: What is the NCO support channel?
a: The channel from the SMA down to the first-line leader. It parallels and reinforces the chain of command. NCOs use it to pass information, standards, and individual training and welfare issues. AR 600-20, Ch 2.

q: Why is it important to know your chain of command?
a: So you know who gives orders and who is responsible, and so issues get routed to the right level.

q: What's the difference between the chain of command and the NCO support channel?
a: The chain of command issues orders and holds command authority. The NCO support channel backs up the chain, focusing on standards, training and Soldier care.

q: Who is the senior enlisted leader of 4ID?
a: The Division CSM. name.

q: Who was the first Sergeant Major of the Army?
a: SMA William O. Wooldridge, 1966.

q: What is the "Backbone of the Army"?
a: The NCO Corps.

q: What is the NCO Guide?
a: TC 7-22.7, The Noncommissioned Officer Guide.

q: Where do you see yourself in 5 years?
a: A realistic goal: squad leader and SSG, ALC complete, college progress, and developing Soldiers.

q: What makes a good team leader?
a: Leading by example, knowing your Soldiers, enforcing standards consistently, and training your team to be ready to take your job.

q: What is the Army's mission?
a: To deploy, fight, and win our Nation's wars by providing ready, prompt, and sustained land dominance by Army forces across the full spectrum of conflict as part of the joint force.

q: How many Soldiers are in a fire team? A squad?
a: A fire team has 4. A squad has 9: the squad leader and two fire teams.

q: What's the difference between a CPL and a SPC?
a: Both are E-4. The CPL is an NCO with NCO authority and responsibilities. The SPC is not.

q: What are the three Army components?
a: Regular Army, Army National Guard, Army Reserve.

q: What does the flag stand for?
a: 13 stripes for the original colonies. 50 stars for the states.

q: What do you do when the anthem plays outdoors and you're in uniform?
a: Face the flag or the music, stand at attention, and salute from the first note to the last.

q: Define leadership.
a: Influencing people by providing purpose, direction, and motivation to accomplish the mission and improve the organization.

q: Name the three leader attributes and the three competencies.
a: Attributes: Character, Presence, Intellect. Competencies: Leads, Develops, Achieves.

q: What are the three categories of counseling?
a: Performance, professional growth, and event.

q: What form is used for counseling? For a SGT's NCOER?
a: DA Form 4856. DA Form 2166-9-1.

q: When should you do an initial counseling?
a: When a Soldier first arrives (reception and integration), and within the first 30 days of a rating period. AR 623-3

q: What are the levels of leadership?
a: Direct, organizational, and strategic. A team leader works at the direct level. ADP 6-22.

q: What's the difference between counseling, coaching and mentoring?
a: Counseling: a leader and subordinate review performance and potential. Coaching: guiding someone to improve a specific skill. Mentoring: a voluntary, long-term relationship between someone more experienced and someone less experienced, for development.

q: What should a counseling plan of action include?
a: Specific actions, who is responsible, and a deadline, so the Soldier knows exactly what to do to improve.

q: What is the NCOER rating chain for a SGT?
a: Rater, senior rater, and supplementary reviewer, if one applies. AR 623-3.

q: What does it mean to lead by example?
a: Meeting every standard you enforce: PT, appearance, timeliness. Soldiers do what they see.

q: What regulation covers Army Command Policy?
What is AER?
a: Army Emergency Relief. It provides financial help to Soldiers and their families. AR 930-4.

q: What do BOSS and MWR stand for?
a: Better Opportunities for Single Soldiers; Morale, Welfare, and Recreation.

q: What does a flag do?
a: It suspends favorable personnel actions such as promotion, awards, and schools. AR 600-8-2.

q: What article of the UCMJ covers nonjudicial punishment?
a: Article 15.

q: What regulation covers leave?
a: AR 600-8-10. Soldiers earn 2.5 days per month.

q: What does a flag do to promotions?
a: It suspends favorable actions, including promotion. AR 600-8-2.

q: What are the types of discharge?
a: Administrative: honorable, general, other than honorable. Punitive (court-martial only): bad conduct and dishonorable.

q: Can a Soldier be punished for self-referring to ASAP?
a: Self-referral is encouraged and handled differently from command or test-based referrals. AR 600-85 limited use policy.

q: What article covers sexual assault?
a: Article 120, UCMJ.

q: What regulation covers SHARP?
What are the two reporting options for sexual assault?
a: Restricted and unrestricted. A SARC or VA explains eligibility and exceptions.

q: What form records a sexual harassment complaint?
a: DA Form 7746.

q: What form is used for a formal EO complaint?
a: DA Form 7279.

q: What does ACE stand for?
a: Ask, Care, Escort.

q: Who is your unit SARC/VA and EOL?
a: Know the names and where the contact info is posted on the company board.

q: Who can take a restricted report?
a: A SARC, a SHARP VA, or healthcare personnel. AR 600-52 para 3-3.

q: What is retaliation?
a: Taking or threatening adverse action, ostracism or maltreatment against someone for reporting. It's prohibited. AR 600-52 Ch 9.

q: Who is your SHARP representative?
a: Know your SARC and VA by name and where their info is posted.

q: What are the warning signs of suicide?
a: Talking about death or hopelessness, giving away possessions, withdrawing, increased alcohol use, sudden mood changes, and relationship, legal or financial trouble.

q: What is the regulation for wear and appearance?
a: AR 670-1, with wear details in DA Pam 670-1.

q: What chapter of AR 670-1 covers grooming?
a: Chapter 3.

q: What is the facial hair standard?
a: Clean-shaven in uniform or on duty unless an approved medical exception or religious accommodation applies.

q: Where do ribbons go on your AGSU coat?
a: Centered 1/8 inch above the left breast pocket, highest precedence on the wearer's right.

q: What are the three 4ID tactical uniform configurations?
a: Ivy Duty, Ivy Light, Ivy Ready (4ID Green Book).

q: Where is the nameplate worn on your AGSU?
a: Know the exact answer from DA Pam 670-1 for your uniform and be ready to show it.

q: Can Soldiers wear wireless earbuds in uniform?
a: Check the current AR 670-1 and Army Directive updates. Don't answer from memory.

q: Who is responsible for a Soldier's appearance?
a: The Soldier first, then first-line leaders who inspect and correct.

q: What regulation covers enlisted promotions?
a: AR 600-8-19, Enlisted Promotions and Demotions.

q: What is the ABCP pass standard?
a: Waist divided by height must be less than 0.550. 0.550 fails. (AD 2026-13)

q: Does a high AFT score exempt a Soldier from ABCP?
a: No.

q: What form records the body composition assessment?
a: DA Form 5500.

q: What's the difference between the primary and secondary zone?
a: The primary zone has longer TIS and TIG requirements. The secondary zone lets top performers be recommended earlier, at the commander's discretion.

q: What system tracks promotion points now?
a: IPPS-A, the Integrated Personnel and Pay System–Army.

q: What is the highest award for valor?
a: The Medal of Honor.

q: What form is a recommendation for award?
a: DA Form 638.

q: Name the five H2F domains.
a: Physical, nutritional, mental, spiritual, and sleep readiness.

q: Name the five AFT events.
a: Deadlift, hand-release push-up, sprint-drag-carry, plank, two-mile run.

q: What's the AFT combat standard?
a: 350 total points with at least 60 on each event.

q: Does a CFT failure in November 2026 trigger adverse action?
a: Not on its own. AD 2026-07 gives a one-year implementation period from 17 Apr 2026.

q: What are the last three exercises of the Recovery Drill?
a: Groin Stretch, Calf Stretch, Hamstring Stretch.

q: What does H2F stand for?
a: Holistic Health and Fitness.

q: What are the first three Preparation Drill exercises?
a: Bend and Reach, Rear Lunge, High Jumper.

q: What does the AFT minimum per event mean for you?
a: As 11B, I need at least 60 on each event and 350 total under the combat standard.

q: Who is on the H2F performance team?
a: Strength coaches, athletic trainers, physical therapists, dietitians, and cognitive performance specialists.

q: A Soldier wants to start college. Where do you send them?
a: To the Education Center to set up Tuition Assistance through ArmyIgnitED. It's governed by AR 621-5.

q: What does the government contribute under BRS?
a: 1% automatically, plus matching up to 5% total when the Soldier contributes 5% to the TSP.

q: What's the maximum SGLI coverage?
What does ATC stand for in MRT?
a: Activating event, Thoughts, Consequences.

q: Name the six MRT competencies.
a: Self-awareness, self-regulation, optimism, mental agility, strengths of character, connection.

q: Where can a Soldier get confidential counseling with no records?
a: The chaplain (privileged communication) or an MFLC.

q: Name the 8-step training model.
a: Plan; train and certify leaders; recon the site; issue the order; rehearse; execute; conduct the AAR; retrain.

q: What are the four parts of an AAR?
a: What was supposed to happen, what happened, why it happened, and what to sustain or improve.

q: What are the five steps of risk management?
a: Identify hazards; assess hazards; develop controls and make risk decisions; implement controls; supervise and evaluate.

q: What form documents a deliberate risk assessment?
a: DD Form 2977.

q: What do you wear in MOPP 4?
a: Everything: overgarment, boots, mask and gloves.

q: What regulation covers OPSEC?
List the eight TLPs.
a: Receive the mission; issue a WARNORD; make a tentative plan; initiate movement; conduct reconnaissance; complete the plan; issue the order; supervise and refine.

q: What are the five paragraphs of an OPORD?
a: Situation, Mission, Execution, Sustainment, Command and Signal.

q: When do you use bounding overwatch?
a: When enemy contact is expected.

q: What does the U in SALUTE stand for?
a: Unit.

q: What is a WARNORD?
a: A warning order gives subordinates early information so they can start preparing.

q: What ATP covers the Stryker platoon and squad?
What's the form for recording vehicle faults?
a: DA Form 5988-E.

q: What are the four steps of a battle drill react to contact?
a: React, locate, suppress, and then the leader decides to assault, flank or break contact. ATP 3-21.8.

q: What's the difference between cover and concealment?
a: Cover protects you from fire. Concealment only hides you from observation.

q: What are the three types of patrols?
a: Combat, reconnaissance, and security patrols.

q: What are the forms of maneuver?
a: Envelopment, flank attack, frontal attack, infiltration, penetration, turning movement. ADP 3-90.

q: What is a team leader's role in a Stryker squad dismount?
a: Control the fire team, keep it in formation and contact, and execute the squad leader's plan.

q: What is an ORP?
a: Objective Rally Point. It's where the unit halts out of sight, sound and small-arms range of the objective to make final preparations.

q: What's the difference between CASEVAC and MEDEVAC?
a: MEDEVAC uses a dedicated medical platform with medical care en route. CASEVAC uses any available, non-medical vehicle.

q: What is a FRAGORD?
a: A fragmentary order, which changes an existing order.

q: What does LD stand for?
a: Line of Departure. It's where the attack begins and is crossed at a set time.

q: What are PCCs and PCIs?
a: Pre-combat checks and pre-combat inspections. Leaders confirm Soldiers and equipment are ready before the mission.

q: What is an FPL?
a: A Final Protective Line: the line where a machine gun's grazing fire stops an enemy assault.

q: Name the four functional elements of the shot process.
a: Stability, aim, control, and movement.

q: What are the three phases of the shot process?
a: Pre-shot, shot, and post-shot.

q: What is the max effective range of the M4 for a point target?
a: 500 meters (area 600 m), per TC 3-22.9.

q: How much does the M240B weigh?
a: 27.1 pounds, per TC 3-22.240 Table 2-1.

q: Why verify a range figure against the platform?
a: Because it varies with weapon variant, firing support (bipod or tripod), ammunition, and configuration.

q: What are the four rules of weapon safety?
a: Treat every weapon as loaded; never point it at anything you don't intend to shoot; keep your finger off the trigger until ready to fire; keep the weapon on safe until you intend to fire.

q: What are the 8 steps of the cycle of function?
a: Feeding, chambering, locking, firing, unlocking, extracting, ejecting, cocking.

q: What magnification is your ACOG?
a: 4x (M150 RCO).

q: Tell me about your weapon.
a: M4 carbine, 5.56 mm, gas-operated, air-cooled, magazine-fed, shoulder-fired. 500 m point, 600 m area. Your optic and zero. TC 3-22.9.

q: What are the two attack modes of the Javelin?
a: Top attack and direct attack.

q: What does TOW stand for?
a: Tube-launched, Optically tracked, Wire-guided.

q: What is the kill radius of an M67 grenade?
a: 5 meters. The casualty radius is 15 meters.

q: What is written on the front of a Claymore?
a: "FRONT TOWARD ENEMY."

q: What mortar does the Stryker MCV carry?
a: The M121 120 mm mortar.

q: What's the max effective range of the AT4?
a: About 300 meters.

q: What does PMCS stand for, and what are the intervals?
a: Preventive Maintenance Checks and Services. Before, during, after, weekly, and monthly.

q: What form is used to record faults?
a: DA Form 5988-E. DA Form 2404 is the manual version.

q: What's the difference between ROGER and WILCO?
a: ROGER means I received it. WILCO means I received it, understand it, and will comply.

q: What does PACE stand for?
a: Primary, Alternate, Contingency, Emergency.

q: What is a hand receipt?
a: DA Form 2062. It shows who is responsible for property.

q: What does SINCGARS stand for?
a: Single Channel Ground and Airborne Radio System.

q: What replaced TC 4-02.1?
a: ATP 4-02.11, Casualty Response, Tactical Combat Casualty Care, and First Aid.

q: Name the three phases of TCCC.
a: Care Under Fire, Tactical Field Care, Tactical Evacuation Care.

q: What does MARCH stand for?
a: Massive hemorrhage, Airway, Respiration, Circulation, Hypothermia/Head injury.

q: What is line 1 of a 9-line?
a: Location of the pickup site.

q: Where do you place a tourniquet in Care Under Fire?
a: High and tight on the injured limb. ATP 4-02.11.

q: What is the most preventable cause of death on the battlefield?
a: Bleeding from an extremity (massive hemorrhage).

q: What's in your IFAK?
a: Know your issued contents: tourniquet, pressure dressing, hemostatic gauze, nasopharyngeal airway, chest seal, etc.

q: What does precedence A, Urgent, mean?
a: Evacuate within 1 hour.

q: Name the five major terrain features.
a: Hill, saddle, valley, ridge, depression.

q: Minor and supplementary?
a: Minor: draw, spur, cliff. Supplementary: cut, fill.

q: An 8-digit grid is accurate to how many meters?
a: 10 meters.

q: What are the three norths?
a: True, magnetic, and grid north.

q: What is the scale of a standard military map?
What do you use to determine your location?
a: Resection, using two or more known points.

q: How many mils in a circle?
What manual covers drill and ceremonies?
What regulation covers salutes and honors?
a: AR 600-25, Salutes, Honors, and Courtesy.

q: What are the two parts of most drill commands?
a: The preparatory command and the command of execution.

q: How long is a quick-time step, and at what cadence?
a: 30 inches at 120 steps per minute.

q: Name the four rest positions.
a: Parade rest, stand at ease, at ease, rest.

q: When do you not salute?
a: Indoors (except when formally reporting), in the field or under tactical conditions, or when both hands are full. AR 600-25.

q: What is the double-time cadence?
a: 180 steps per minute, 30 inches.

q: How was 2-12 Infantry constituted?
a: On 3 May 1861 in the Regular Army as Company B, 1st Battalion, 12th Infantry. Organized 20 Oct 1861 at Fort Hamilton, New York.

q: Who is the most recent Medal of Honor recipient from your company?
a: MAJ (Ret.) Nicholas Dockery, a C Co, 2-12 IN platoon leader in Kapisa Province, Afghanistan. Presented 18 June 2026.

q: What is the 2-12 IN nickname?
a: Lethal Warriors.

q: What brigade are you in, and what is its nickname?
a: 2nd Stryker Brigade Combat Team, "Warhorse."

q: Why the ivy leaf on the 4ID patch?
a: "Ivy" sounds like the Roman numeral IV. Ivy leaves stand for tenacity and fidelity.

q: What makes 4ID unique right now?
a: It's converting to the Army's only all-Stryker infantry division.

q: Where did 4ID land on D-Day?
a: Utah Beach, 6 June 1944. It was the first division ashore there.

q: Who received the Medal of Honor for Utah Beach?
a: BG Theodore Roosevelt Jr.

q: Which 4ID unit captured Saddam Hussein, and when?
a: 4ID Soldiers, near Tikrit, 13 December 2003, during Operation Red Dawn.

q: What were 4ID's three infantry regiments in WWII?
a: The 8th, 12th and 22nd Infantry Regiments.

q: What does OEF stand for? OIF?
a: Operation Enduring Freedom (Afghanistan). Operation Iraqi Freedom (Iraq).

q: When did the Revolutionary War start?
a: 1775. The Army's birthday is 14 June 1775.

q: Your Soldier is late to formation for the second time.
a: Talk to them privately to find out why. Do event counseling on a DA Form 4856 with a plan of action. Apply corrective training if appropriate. Inform your squad leader. Follow up. If it keeps happening, it moves up the chain.

q: A Soldier from another unit walks past you out of uniform standard.
a: Make an on-the-spot correction, professionally and respectfully. Every NCO enforces standards, not just the ones in their own unit.

q: Your Soldier failed the AFT.
a: Find out why: injury, preparation, or effort. Build a plan with them (H2F resources, extra PT). Counsel and document. Follow your chain's policy on flags and retests.

q: Your Soldier failed the ABCP waist-to-height check.
a: Make sure the assessment followed AD 2026-13 (a second team confirmed it, recorded on DA Form 5500). Counsel the Soldier. Connect them with H2F dietitians and trainers. Inform your chain. Be supportive and hold the standard.

q: You smell alcohol on your Soldier at first formation.
a: Remove them from duty and from any weapon or vehicle. Inform your squad leader or PSG right away. The command decides on testing. ASAP referral (AR 600-85). Document it.

q: Your Soldier posted a photo of the vehicle line and the deployment date on social media.
a: Have them take it down right away. Explain the OPSEC risk (AR 530-1). Inform your chain, since it may need to be reported. Counsel and retrain.

q: Your Soldier says, "Sometimes I don't see the point of anything anymore."
a: ACE. Ask directly: "Are you thinking about killing yourself?" Care: listen and take it seriously. Escort: stay with them and take them to Behavioral Health, the chaplain or the ER. Never leave them alone. Inform your chain. If there's immediate danger, call 911.

q: A Soldier tells you they were sexually assaulted.
a: Make sure they're safe and get medical care if needed. Don't promise confidentiality. Tell them you have to report it, and connect them with the SARC or SHARP VA right away. The VA explains restricted and unrestricted reporting. Don't investigate yourself. Protect their privacy. AR 600-52.

q: Your Soldier is being harassed by another Soldier because of their race.
a: Stop the behavior. Make sure the victim is safe. Inform your chain. Explain the EO complaint options: informal, or formal on DA Form 7279. Connect them with the unit EOL. Protect them from retaliation. AR 600-20 Ch 6.

q: Your Soldier can't pay rent this month.
a: Find out the cause. AER for emergency assistance. ACS financial readiness counseling. Help them build a budget. Follow up next payday.

q: Your Soldier's family member is in the hospital back home.
a: Inform your chain right away for emergency leave. Red Cross message. AER for travel funds if needed. Check on them while they're gone.

q: A new Soldier just arrived on your team.
a: Sponsor them. Do the initial counseling within the first 30 days. Learn their background, goals and family situation. Get them through in-processing, issue and training. Pair them with a battle buddy.

q: You get an order you think is unsafe.
a: Bring your concern to the leader who gave it, respectfully, with facts and risk-management steps. If it's lawful, execute it with controls in place. If it's clearly illegal, do not obey, and report it through the chain.

q: Your squad leader is gone and the PSG gives your team a mission.
a: Acknowledge it and back-brief. Use the TLPs: issue a WARNORD, plan, inspect (PCCs/PCIs), execute. Report completion. "Initiative by taking appropriate action in the absence of orders." (NCO Creed)

q: Two of your Soldiers keep arguing and it's affecting the team.
a: Separate them and talk to each one individually. Find the root cause. Mediate. Set clear expectations. Counsel if needed. Inform your squad leader if it keeps happening.

q: Your team is behind on PMCS before a field problem.
a: Prioritize: get the vehicle and weapons mission-capable first. Divide the tasks by who knows what. Inform the chain about deadline faults early, not at the last minute. Do an AAR afterward so it doesn't happen again.

q: Your friend from your old team is now your Soldier.
a: Have the conversation early. Explain the relationship has changed professionally. Enforce the same standard for everyone. Avoid any appearance of favoritism (AR 600-20 / AR 600-32).

q: You made a mistake that affected the mission.
a: Own it right away. Tell your leader what happened and what you're doing to fix it. Learn from it in the AAR. Integrity matters more than looking good.

q: Your team makes contact on a patrol.
a: Return fire and take cover. Locate the enemy. Send a SALUTE report. Gain fire superiority. Follow the battle drill (react to contact) and the squad leader's direction. Send a LACE report after contact.

q: A Soldier on your team is wounded under fire.
a: Care Under Fire: win the fight first. Direct the casualty to self-aid and cover. Once it's safe, apply a tourniquet if there's massive bleeding. Move to Tactical Field Care (MARCH). Request MEDEVAC with a 9-line.

q: You find a suspected IED on your route.
a: Stop. Don't touch it. Confirm from a distance. Clear the area. Cordon it off. Check for secondary devices. Control the area. Report with a 9-line UXO/IED report. the 5 Cs: Confirm, Clear, Call, Cordon, Control.

q: Correct this: 1-12 IN lineage (Co A, 1st Bn)
a: 2-12 IN: constituted 3 May 1861 as Company B, 1st Bn, 12th Infantry

q: Correct this: SALUTE: U = Uniform
a: U = Unit

q: Correct this: OPORD para 5 = Command and Control
a: Para 5 = Command and Signal

q: Correct this: TC 4-02.1 is first aid
a: ATP 4-02.11 (23 Mar 2026) superseded it

q: Correct this: FM 3-25.26 land nav
Correct this: FM 27-2 physical fitness
a: FM 7-22 and ATP 7-22.02

q: Correct this: 3rd TCCC phase: "combat casualty evac plan"
a: Tactical Evacuation Care

q: Correct this: Recovery Drill items 6 and 7 swapped
a: 6 = Groin Stretch, 7 = Calf Stretch

q: Correct this: Shot process: "steady position, aiming, breathing, trigger squeeze"
a: Stability, Aim, Control, Movement

q: Correct this: AR 600-20 is the SHARP reg
Correct this: AR 600-63 is suicide prevention
a: AR 600-92. AR 600-63 is Army Health Promotion.

q: Correct this: DA Form 5501 for tape
a: DA Form 5500 only. 5501 is no longer used.

q: Correct this: ADP 6-22 = "Army Talent Management"
a: ADP 6-22 = Army Leadership and the Profession
